page: Microsoft Azure F2alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is driven by 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration features a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio, providing 4.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per core) and 32 MB of L3 cache. Storage needs are supported by a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD, and the platform includes vector acceleration via AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16 instruction sets without dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark measurements highlight strong single-core CPU capabilities. In stress-ng single-core testing, the instance registers in the top tier (3770.27), complemented by top-tier single-threaded gzip compression at 40.66 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 18.02 GB/sec. Multi-core performance scales linearly across its two dedicated threads, delivering average stress-ng throughput (7534.96) and a PassMark CPU score of 6893.20. Memory bandwidth reaches 52.81 GB/sec on large uncached read transfers, though the constrained 4.0 GB capacity limits multi-threaded decompression and results in below-average overall PassMark memory scores.

Cost efficiency is focused around single-threaded processing speed and integrated local NVMe storage rather than total memory capacity. The primary tradeoff is the lean 2.0 GB per core memory ceiling, making the instance unsuitable for large in-memory caching or high-concurrency database systems. Microsoft Azure F2alds_v7 is best fitted for compute-bound single-thread workloads, CI/CD build stages, batch compression pipelines, and utility microservices requiring high clock frequency and fast temporary scratch disk space.
description: Microsoft Azure F2alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine utilizing the x86_64 architecture with 2 dedicated cores and 2 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor at 4.5 GHz. Built with a 1:2 core-to-memory configuration, it integrates 4.0 GB of system memory alongside 236 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, operating without discrete GPUs. In synthetic benchmarking, the instance demonstrates top-tier single-threaded performance in stress-ng and compression tests, supported by AVX-512 instruction extensions. Multi-threaded metrics and memory benchmarks fall into moderate tiers due to the dual-thread ceiling and modest memory footprint. Qualitative cost efficiency is realized through strong single-core computing density and bundled high-speed disk access rather than expansive memory capacity. The server is well suited for CPU-focused single-threaded execution, continuous integration workers, batch data compression, and lightweight edge compute workloads.
